summary: COP31 ends without a deal, NATO meets over missiles in Poland, Iran hits Bahrain again, AI stocks wobble, OpenAI floats AI limits, and Congo's Ebola outbreak grows.

question.text: COP31 failed because a few countries could block a deal everyone else wanted. If more countries now act in smaller groups instead of waiting for all 200 to agree, what might be gained, and what might be lost for the countries left out?

read.title: Data centers full of U.S. chips are serving Chinese AI models–undermining Trump's tech ambitions
read.summary: Researchers at Georgetown's CSET explain how Chinese AI models end up running on American chips abroad, why new US rules target that, and what they think would work better.

topics.heading: COP31 ends without a deal after countries reject a text that skips fossil fuels
topics.summary: The UN climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, closed on Sunday without agreeing its main decision, after two extra days of talks.[^1][^2] The EU, the UK, Norway and several island states refused a final text that did not name coal, oil or gas; reports call it the first COP to end this way since Copenhagen in 2009.[^1][^3]

lead.title: COP31 climate talks collapse as EU and others reject deal

alsoReported.title: UN climate conference ends without its signature agreement as countries clash over fossil fuels and finance
COP31 in Turkey collapses without deal as EU rejects text silent on fossil fuels

article: Yesterday's brief left COP31 in overtime. On Sunday it ended without the "cover decision", the main text that sums up what nearly 200 countries agree to do next.[^1] The summit's Turkish president, Murat Kurum, told delegates there was no agreement and that he would not put forward another text. "We did our best," he said.[^1][^2]

The final draft did not name oil, gas or coal and set no phase-out, referring only back to the 2023 Dubai pledge.[^1] An earlier target of $120 billion for adaptation, meaning money to help countries cope with floods, heat and drought, was replaced by a promise to discuss "at least tripling" adaptation money by 2035, with no starting figure.[^1][^3] The text also accepted that warming is on course to pass 1.5C.[^3]

Ireland's minister, speaking for the EU, called the text "unconscionable" and said the summit was "hijacked by some oil states".[^1][^2] Panama, the Marshall Islands, Vanuatu and Tuvalu also refused it; Tuvalu's negotiator said "it seems like we are negotiating with the Saudis".[^3] Saudi Arabia defended carbon capture, which traps CO2 before it reaches the air, saying climate change "requires all solutions on the table". China backed the text, and bne IntelliNews reports India did too.[^1][^3] UN Secretary-General António Guterres said he was "deeply disappointed".[^2]

Background: COP decisions need consensus, so any bloc can block a deal. This year the presidency was split between Türkiye and Australia, whose minister Chris Bowen called the outcome "very disappointing".[^2][^3] Some decisions were still made: at least 75 countries joined a voluntary pledge to raise electricity's share of energy use to 35% by 2035, from about 23% today.[^1]

My read: a COP without a cover text does not undo the Paris Agreement, and countries' own plans still matter most. But it shows how hard it has become to agree even on words. The next summit is in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in November 2027.[^1]
topics.differences: Lists of who backed the text differ: ABC News names China and Ghana, while bne IntelliNews names China and India.[^1][^3] Supporters of the text, including Saudi Arabia, frame carbon capture as a practical solution; island states and the EU say the text gave it special treatment while dropping fossil-fuel language.[^1][^3]

topics.heading: NATO meets over Russian missiles in Poland as Ukraine says it sank a Russian ship
topics.summary: NATO ambassadors meet in Brussels on Monday after two Russian missiles and a drone came down in Poland on Nov 20; Polish prosecutors say they found Kh-101 cruise missile debris at three sites.[^4][^5] A Russian drone strike near Kyiv killed at least 10, and Ukraine says it sank a Russian warship off Libya.[^6][^7]

lead.title: NATO emergency talks on tap as US commander assess defenses after Russian missiles hit Poland

alsoReported.title: Polish authorities find Russian missile remains at three sites following airspace incursion
'No safe routes' — Ukraine sinks Russian corvette in drone attack off Libyan coast

article: On Nov 20, during one of Russia's largest strikes on Ukraine, two missiles and a jet-powered drone came down in southeastern Poland. No one was hurt.[^4] Polish prosecutors say they have found remains of Kh-101 cruise missiles at three sites and that initial findings suggest they were built in recent weeks in Dubna, Russia.[^5] A Swedish fighter pilot under NATO command was cleared to shoot one down but did not fire, because bad weather made it impossible to identify the target.[^5]

Polish officials say the North Atlantic Council, NATO's main decision body, meets on Monday and that Poland will bring proposals for stronger defences. Poland has asked for more surveillance aircraft and F-35 jets.[^4] NATO's secretary general, Mark Rutte, said in Warsaw that "NATO will defend every inch of Polish territory." Poland's defence minister noted that one missile fell about 35 km from a site where European troops were training, and said that was "hard to regard" as a coincidence.[^4] No Russian response was reported.[^4][^5]

Inside Ukraine, a drone strike destroyed part of an apartment block in Dymer, north of Kyiv, early on Nov 22. Officials say at least 10 people died; a 7-year-old boy was pulled out alive after almost 14 hours.[^6] Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelensky, says his navy used seven sea drones to sink the Russian corvette Merkury off Libya. That claim has not been independently confirmed.[^7]
On peace talks, nothing new was agreed this weekend. Zelensky said he has not seen US security guarantees "on paper" and wants them to last "preferably forever".[^8]

What to watch: whether NATO's meeting leads to new deployments over Poland. My read: the alliance is likely to strengthen air defence rather than respond militarily, but each incident raises the cost of a mistake.
topics.differences: Ukraine says it sank the Merkury; Russia has not commented, and the damage has not been checked independently.[^7] Death tolls in Dymer rose through the day, and figures may still change.[^6]

topics.heading: Iran hits Bahrain again and says Hormuz can be safe only if the US meets its terms
topics.summary: Bahrain says an Iranian attack hit an industrial site on Nov 21, and Gulf neighbours condemned it.[^9][^10] Iran says the Strait of Hormuz can be made safe if the US lifts sanctions and its naval blockade, while President Trump says he may wait until the new year before deciding on new strikes.[^9][^10]

lead.title: Iran live updates: Tehran says Strait of Hormuz will be safe if its demands are met

alsoReported.title: Live Updates: Trump says he wants 'permanent' deal with Iran; warns next move may not come until 2027
US weighs delaying Iran strikes despite Israeli pressure for military action

article: Bahrain says an Iranian attack on Saturday, Nov 21, started a fire at a civilian industrial site in Sitra and injured two people. Bahrain called it the fourth attempted Iranian attack in about a week.[^9][^10] Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar and the UAE condemned it; Qatar called it a "flagrant violation" of Bahrain's sovereignty.[^9][^10]

At sea, the UK's maritime agency UKMTO reported incidents involving tankers near Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) say two tankers hit sea mines while using "unauthorized routes", and claim they shot down a US drone. The US military had not commented.[^9][^10] Iran International reports seven tankers have been hit in the strait since Nov 16.[^11]

Background: since the war began this year, the US has blockaded Iranian ports and Iran has restricted shipping through Hormuz, the narrow channel through which a large share of the world's oil passes. On Monday, Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said security "can be restored" there if the US lifts sanctions, ends the blockade and carries out a memorandum agreed in June. He said Iran "will under no circumstances back down".[^9]

In Washington, President Trump told Fox News he would not let Iran have a nuclear weapon, but told Israeli TV he is "not rushing" and could wait until the new year.[^10] Iran International, citing other reports, says Israel is pressing for renewed strikes while the UK and some Gulf states have privately urged restraint.[^11] A Qatari delegation held talks in Tehran.[^10]

My read: the most likely path is more weeks of slow, risky standoff at sea. Watch whether Qatar's mediation produces any meeting, and whether the US funding fight in Congress, due by Dec 11, touches the war.
topics.differences: Bahrain's interior ministry and ABC News say two people were injured; CBS News reported no injuries.[^9][^10] Iran says tankers hit mines on routes it had not approved; other reports describe attacks, and whether these are the same incidents is unclear.[^9][^10]

topics.heading: Asian chip stocks keep falling while US futures bounce after Friday's AI-led rout
topics.summary: South Korea's Kospi fell 3.3% on Monday while US stock futures rose about 2%, after Friday's AI-led sell-off.[^12][^13] Over the weekend, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned the Federal Reserve against raising rates too far.[^14]

lead.title: Asian stock markets tumble as AI bubble fears mount

alsoReported.title: US futures climb and Asian shares mostly decline as some tech stocks fall
Europe's STOXX 600 rises as tech shares rebound after AI-driven rout

article: On Friday, Nov 20, the S&P 500 fell 3.7% and slipped into a "correction", meaning more than 10% below its peak. The Nasdaq fell 5.3% and is now down for the year. Nvidia, under scrutiny since its founder's exit and a reported SEC look at its accounting, fell 14%.[^13]

On Monday, Asia was mixed. South Korea's Kospi fell as much as 5.8% before closing 3.3% lower, with chipmakers Samsung and SK Hynix down. Taiwan's market rose 2.2%, and Japan was closed for a holiday.[^12][^13] US futures, which show where stocks may open, were up about 2% for the S&P 500 and about 3% for the Nasdaq, and European stocks rose 0.7% in early trading.[^12][^15] One analyst warned the bounce "could be a dead cat bounce", a brief rise inside a longer fall.[^15]

Why it matters: huge sums are flowing into AI chips and data centres. Gartner, cited by Al Jazeera, expects $2.7 trillion of AI investment this year. Investors are asking whether the profits will justify that.[^12] South Korea and Taiwan depend heavily on chip exports, so they feel these swings first.[^12]

Interest rates are the other worry. Bessent said on CBS on Sunday that the Fed "may be making a policy mistake if they over-tighten", meaning raise rates too far. Markets expect a rate rise at the Fed's Dec 9 meeting.[^14] Higher rates make borrowing costlier for families and firms, and tend to weigh on stock prices.[^14]
This is a judgment: one strong day would not settle whether the AI boom is a bubble. This week's US inflation data and the Fed's December decision will matter more.
topics.differences: Some investors see the drop as a healthy correction after a long rise; others, quoted by Reuters and Al Jazeera, fear further falls if AI spending does not pay off.[^12][^15] Bessent links the fall partly to Democratic election gains and the Fed's tone, a view his political opponents would dispute.[^14]

topics.heading: OpenAI's chief scientist proposes shared industry limits on how capable AI can get
topics.summary: OpenAI's chief scientist, Jakub Pachocki, proposed that AI developers agree on common limits tied to a measure of model ability, and not cross them until safety research catches up.[^16][^17] CEO Sam Altman praised the idea; US governors also published principles for sharing AI rules between states and Washington.[^16][^18]

lead.title: OpenAI's chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development

alsoReported.title: OpenAI scientist proposes industry AI limits tied to model intelligence metric
Governors Want States to Have a Voice in Regulating AI

article: In a blog post on Sunday, OpenAI's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki called for "common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements". Developers would promise not to build models past a limit until the ability to monitor and understand AI behaviour reaches a set milestone.[^16]

Perplexity is a number that measures how well a model predicts text: lower means better. Pachocki argues that test scores for specific skills quickly go out of date, while perplexity stays useful as "a shared benchmark for general intelligence". He links certain levels of it to the appearance of new abilities in areas like maths and cybersecurity.[^17] He warns AI could start speeding up its own training methods "as early as 2027", possibly faster than safety work.[^16]

OpenAI's CEO Sam Altman called it "the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while."[^16] TechCrunch notes that Anthropic's CEO, Dario Amodei, has made a similar call to "pace the frontier".[^17] So far it is a proposal, not an agreement: no other company has signed on, and no government has adopted it.[^16][^17]

Separately, the US National Governors Association released principles for a "shared national approach" to AI, ahead of the new Congress in January. It says Washington should handle national and international risks, while states keep the right to set rules for AI used in their own services.[^18]

Why it matters: rules for powerful AI are being argued over in companies, states, Washington and the UN at once. My read: voluntary limits are easier to promise than to keep when rivals keep racing, so watch whether other labs or governments take the idea up.

topics.heading: WHO keeps Congo's Ebola outbreak a global emergency as cases pass 11,600
topics.summary: The World Health Organization says Congo's Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, had reached 11,613 confirmed cases and 5,678 deaths by Nov 17, and remains a public health emergency of international concern.[^19] It is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record.[^20]

lead.title: Ebola Outbreak Climbs to 11,645 Cases as Deaths Near 5700

alsoReported.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus - Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya and Nigeria

article: The WHO's latest report says that as of Nov 17 the Democratic Republic of the Congo had 11,613 confirmed Ebola cases and 5,678 deaths, in 68 health zones across 8 provinces. About half of confirmed patients have died.[^19] On Nov 18 the WHO's director-general confirmed it is still a "public health emergency of international concern", the agency's highest alarm.[^19]

Cases have also appeared elsewhere. Kenya has had 9 cases and 2 deaths, and is counting down 42 days, twice the virus's longest incubation period, since its last patient left hospital. Nigeria's single imported case recovered.[^19] Using US CDC data, Contagion Live counts 11,645 cases in all countries, 500 more than a week earlier, and says it is the second-largest Ebola outbreak ever.[^20]

Background: this outbreak, declared in May, is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a type of Ebola for which the WHO says "no approved vaccines or specific treatments currently exist". Two candidate vaccines are entering a trial, and a treatment trial is under way.[^19] Fighting in eastern Congo, attacks on health workers and shortages of protective gear make the response harder.[^20]
Why it matters: the WHO rates the risk as very high in Congo but low globally.[^19] The US has barred travellers who were in Congo in the past 21 days from commercial flights to the US.[^20]
My read: with about 500 new cases a week and active spread in 48 health zones, an end is not yet in sight.[^19][^20] Watch the vaccine trial results.
